trivia.wildlifeexplorers.dissostichus_el: The Chilean Sea Bass, also known as the Patagonian Toothfish is an icefish that lives in the southern cold oceans at depths of 45 to over 3000 meters deep.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.percophis_brasi: The Brazilian Flathead is considered to be the most basal member of Notothenioidei. It lives off the coast of Brazil and Argentina.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.eleginops_maclo: The Patagonian Blennie is known to live in estuarine and coastal habitats off Argentina and Chile.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.pseudaphritis_u: The Congoli is a fish endemic to the estuaries of south Australia. It is a carnivorous ambush predator.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.betta_splendens: The Betta fish is a popular aquarium trade fish known for the striking colors and patterns it can have. The wild forms are duller in appearance.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.synbranchus_mar: The marbled swamp eel is a nocturnal predator that sometimes burrows into the ground to find concealed animals. It burrows deeper during drier periods to stay below the water table.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.chaudhuria_caud: This animal is around 6cm in length, and does not possess scales. Very little is known about their habits or their biology. Both the dorsal and anal fins lack spines.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.mastacembelus_a: The Zig-zag Eel, or Tire-track eel is a freshwater spiny eel native to South and Southeast Asia. They are popular in the aquarium trade for their striking patterns and color.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.mastacembelus_e: The Fire Eel is a large spiny eel, able to grow up to 1 meter in length. They live in slow-moving rivers along the muddy substrate, and are native to Southeast Asia.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.macrognathus_si: The Peacock Eel is native to the Mekong basin and lives near the riverbed. They burrow into the substrate to hunt for invertebrates or hide from predators.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.mastacembelus_b: Blind Spiny Eels are a rare species of Mastacembelus found in the Congo River. They typically prey on small invertebrates. As they are blind, they use their strong senses to hunt.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.sinobdella_sine: This species is native to southern China, Taiwan, and Vietnam. It is moderately sized, growing up to 38cm in total length. They prey on small invertebrates.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.rakthamichthys_: These are blind swamp eels endemic to India. They live underground, in streams throughout caves. This fish has a bright red coloration and incredibly reduced eyes.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.nematistius_pec: Roosterfish are fast-moving pelagic predators with uniquely long spines on their dorsal fins. They are large, able to reach over 1.6m in length and are a popular sport fish.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.toxotes_chatare: Archerfish are able to spit streams of water to knock insects into the water. They are able to hit distances of over 1m. Their diet typically consists of zooplankton and invertebrates.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.pogonophryne_ma: This species of plunderfish is found in cold and deep antarctic waters. They have a flattened head and a mental barbel, which it uses as a sensory mechanism to find prey.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.chaenocephalus_: The blackfin icefish lives on the Antarctic continental shelf. They have translucent blood and they lack haemoglobin. Male icefish are known to guard their nests after breeding.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.cygnodraco_maws: This species of dragonfish lives around the Antarctic continental shelf. They are a demersal species that feeds on other smaller fish and invertebrates. They can be found at depths of up to 300m.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.scatophagus_arg: Spotted Scats are omnivorous freshwater to saltwater fish. Despite the name, eating dung has not been confirmed for this species. They can form small schools.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.procambarus_cla: This species of crayfish is dark red and brown in appearance. They are found in warm freshwater ecosystems and can tolerate rather long dry spells.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.procambarus_all: This species of crayfish is popular in the aquarium trade. In the wild it is generally tan-blue, although a selectively bred strain achieves a vibrant blue color.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.procambarus_luc: This species of crayfish is blind and troglomorphic. Its coloration is dull and pinkish and it only lives in caves in Florida.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.procambarus_vir: This species of crayfish is widespread and considered an invasive species as they are able to reproduce via parthenogenesis.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.pangasianodon_g: The Mekong Giant Catfish is a critically endangered large catfish found only in the Mekong River basin. They are toothless and feed on algae.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.naso_brevirostr: These fish have a bony protrusion on their head, giving them the unicorn name. Adults generally feed on zooplankton while juveniles feed on algae.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.pomacanthus_imp: Juvenile Emperor Angelfish are strikingly different from the adults, bearing vibrant blue and white markings. The adults are striped with yellow and blue stripes and a dark mask. It typically eats sponges.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.zanclus_cornutu: Moorish Idols have a high and laterally compressed body with a thin snout. They have small bristle-like teeth they use to feed on corals, tunicates, and other invertebrates. They can be found in small groups
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.paracanthurus_h: Royal Blue Tangs are blue and yellow surgeonfish that are generally found in the Indo-Pacific. They are associated with coral reefs and eat algae that may harm the corals.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.chaetodon_aurig: Threadfin butterflyfish are distributed in the Indo-Pacific region and generally found in shallow coral reefs. They have prominent yellow dorsal fins with a trailing filament and black bands running across its white body.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.chelmon_rostrat: Copperband butterflyfish are usually found in shallow coral reefs in pairs or alone. They have a tube-like mouth used for feeding on small invertebrates such as tubeworms and clams.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.siganus_vulpinu: The foxface rabbitfish is a reef fish found in the Indo-Pacific region. They are omnivorous and are usually found alone or in pairs. At night, the rabbitfish's colors become duller and mottled.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.zebrasoma_flave: The Yellow Tang is a bright yellow surgeonfish that is commonly found in coral reefs. They generally eat algae and at night, a pale white band develops in the middle of their body.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.zebrasoma_velif: The Sailfin Tang is a brown and yellow colored surgeonfish known for its sail-like dorsal and anal fins which it can extend outwards. They generally graze on leafy algae.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.hydrocynus_goli: Goliath Tigerfish is a large fish native to African freshwater environments such as the Congo and Lake Tanganyika. It is a general piscivore but are also known to attack larger animals when food is scarce.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.smutsia_gigante: The giant pangolin is the largest pangolin species at 1.4m in length. It has a strong sense of smell and typically walks with most weight on its columnar legs. Its diet mainly consists of ants and termites.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.indostomus_para: The toothpick fish is a small thin fish that was previously thought to be related to sticklebacks. It is now known to be within Synbranchiformes, related to spiny and swamp eels. They live in slow-moving waters of Indochina.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.cyprinodon_diab: Devil's Hole Pupfish are dark blue and incredibly rare species of pupfish found only in one water-filled cavern in the United States. It is critically endangered with populations fluctuating around 20-50 individuals.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.aenigmachanna_g: This cave dwelling snakehead is very thin and have a very long anal fin. They mostly live in underground caverns and are only found in southwestern India. This animal is considered a relict species.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.satan_eurystomu: The Widemouth Blindcat is a completely blind cave catfish found only in the Edwards Aquifer near San Antonio, Texas. It grows to about 14cm in length and they typically eat crustaceans.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.amblyopsis_hoos: The Hoosier Cavefish is a member of the family Amblyopsidae, a family endemic to the United State' underground caves. This fish has been found only in southern Indiana.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.sinocyclocheilu: This fish is a blind cavefish found only in China. Members of this genus are found both aboveground and underground, with the underground species typically being pinkish in color and blind.
This cavefish is only found in Yunnan, China. It has a upwards pointing horn on its forehead and is also the first ever recorded description of an obligate cavefish.
This cavefish is only found in Guizhou, China. It sports a distinct horn on its forehead that its aboveground relatives lack. They grow to around 13cm in length.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.neolissochilus_: A subterranean cyprinid fish, the blind Mahseer is the current largest cavefish, growing to up to 40cm in length. It is only found in the Indian state of Meghalaya.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.gitchak_nakana: The Gitchak is a small cave loach endemic to Northeast India. It is known from one well. It is translucent and reddish orange in color and it also lacks a skull roof.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.kryptoglanis_sh: This cave catfish is endemic to Kerala, India and has a very long and thin body with a long anal fin. It laks dorsal fins and has an upward pointed mouth.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.munidopsis_poly: The Jameos blind crab is a blind and pale squat lobster found in the caves of Jameos del Agua in the Canary Islands. They are small, only around 3cm long.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.xibalbanus_tulu: Xibalbanus is a venomous remipede known only from caves on the Yucatán Peninsula. It is relatively large for a remipede, being 3cm in length.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.leptobrama_muel: A coastal marine and brackish carangiforme fish, the Beachsalmon is a popular sport fish in Australia and grows to around 38cm in length.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.hippocampus_ing: The pacific seahorse is the largest seahorse, able to grow up to 30cm in height. It is nocturnal and is often found inhabiting seagrass meadows and coral reefs.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.hippocampus_rei: The slender seahorse is small, growing to 17.5cm in height. These seahorses have brown to light spots around their body and typically live near sargassum, seagrass, or corals.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.bovichtus_varie: The thornfish is a small notothenioid fish endemic to New Zealand. It has a brownish, grayish, olive coloration and typically grows to around 25cm in length. They prey on crustaceans and worms.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.heteroconger_ha: The spotted garden eel is a widespread tropical and subtropical fish known to live in variously sized colonies in sandy bottoms. Individuals rarely leave their burrow once they've settled down.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.gorgasia_precla: The splendid garden eel is a medium sized garden eel that mainly lives buried in the sand, with its head and upper body sticking out. They generally live in groups.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.acanthurus_line: The Clown tang is a species of surgeonfish characterized by long blue horizontal stripes across a yellow and white body. This species is found in the Indo-pacific and is generally herbivorous.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.acanthurus_leuc: The Powder blue tang is a surgeonfish found in the Indian Ocean. The intensity of its colors indicates its healthiness, and they generally feed on algae in coral reefs.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.acanthurus_japo: Also known as the Japan surgeonfish, this species of surgeonfish is found around Japan to Indonesia and grows to around 21cm in length. Their appearance is somewhat similar to the White-cheeked surgeonfish.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.acanthurus_soha: The Sohal tang is a striped surgeonfish  found in the Indian Ocean. Sohal comes from the Arabic name for this fish. It grows to around 40cm in length and is usually found alone.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.acanthurus_coer: The Atlantic blue tang is a medium sized surgeonfish found off the coasts of the eastern Americas. They are known to engage in cleaning behavior with other fish and they grow up to 40cm in length.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.acanthurus_achi: The Achilles tang is tropical fish characterized by a large circular orange splotch around its tail spine. It is commonly found in reefs around Hawaii and the Pitcairn Islands.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.forcipiger_flav: This butterflyfish is characterized by its yellow, black and white body colors and long snout. It looks similar to other members of the genus except that its snout is not as long. This animal can reach 22cm in length.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.forcipiger_long: This butterflyfish sports a long slender snout and can be found in the Indo-Pacific region. Its snout is much longer than its cousin, F. flavissimus, which is generally more common and the same size.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.heteroconger_po: The zebra garden eel is a marine tropical eel known from the Indo-Pacific. They form moderately sized colonies and are typically found in very shallow depths.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.heteroconger_lu: The yellow garden eel is a small marine burrowing eel native to the Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico. Their bodies are bright yellow in color.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.gorgasia_barnes: The Barnes' garden eel is one of the largest garden eels, measuring up to 1.2m in length. They live in shallow tropical marine environments off the coast of Indonesia and the western Pacific.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.gorgasia_japoni: The pacific spaghetti eel is a large species of garden eels found in the Western Pacific Ocean. They typically inhabit the seafloor near reefs and form large colonies.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.centropyge_lori: The flame angelfish is a small red, orange, and black fish found around reefs in Oceania. Their diet typically consists of algae and crustaceans.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.centropyge_venu: The purplemask angelfish is named for its yellow and purple color, with a purple splotch on its head giving it the purplemask name. They are found in the Western Pacific, off the coasts of Japan, Taiwan, and the Philippines.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.centropyge_boyl: The peppermint angelfish is a small reef fish native to reefs around the Cook Islands. They typically live around overhangs around the outer slopes of the reefs. Their diet consists of invertebrates.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.hyemoschus_aqua: The water chevrotain is a small deer-like animal that lives in tropical Africa. It is the largest of the chevrotains, at 85cm in length and it typically stays around water, foraging for food. It is also exclusively nocturnal.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.crossarchus_obs: The common kusimanse is a small mongoose-like animal native to West Africa. They are highly social and typically live in large family groups. While capable of climbing, they spend most of their time on the ground.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.muntiacus_muntj: The southern red muntjac is a common species of deer native to Southeast Asia. They are omnivorous, eating fruits, eggs, grass, and occasionally scavenges. Males have canines whereas the females lack canines and antlers.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.crossarchus_pla: The flat-headed kusimanse is a species of kusimanse native to Central Africa. While able to climb, they are mostly terrestrial and often forages in rocks or crevices, looking for termites to eat.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.moschus_moschif: The Siberian musk deer is a small species of deer native to East and North Asia. They mark their territory with fallen branches or defecating. They are generally nocturnal and inhabit the mountainous taigas.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.elaphodus_cepha: The tufted deer is a small deer species characterized by a small tuft of hair on its forehead. They are endemic to higher elevation forests of East and Southeast Asia and are mainly a crepuscular species.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.hystrix_cristat: The crested porcupine is a rodent native to the Mediterranean region and Northern Africa. It sports long quills running along its head, neck, and back, which can be raised. It can rattle the quills on its tail, creating a hiss-like sound.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.ailurus_fulgens: The red panda is a small carnivoran endemic to temperate coniferous forests of Asia. Despite their name, they are not related to the Giant Panda. They are mostly solitary and arboreal.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.galictis_cuja: The lesser grison is a smaller species of mustelid native to South America. they typically inhabit higher elevations in forests. They are carnivorous, and feed mostly on smaller vertebrates.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.galictis_vittat: This animal is a species of mustelid native to Central and South America. They have a long neck and bushy tails and are known to feed on smaller vertebrates. They also respond to threats with short grunts and barks.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.carcharhinus_br: A smaller sized shark, this animal is known for spinning into schools of forage fish in order to feed on them. It grows to a maximum of 3m in length.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.proteus_anguinu: The olm is a cave-dwelling aquatic salamander that is endemic to several caves in Dinaric Alps, mostly in Croatia. It has underdeveloped eyes and and exhibits neoteny, with external gills retained as adults.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.dussumieria_acu: The rainbow sardine is a small schooling forage fish that can be found in the Indo-Pacific regions and the Persian Gulf. It is an important fish to commercial fisheries and typically forms large schools.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.sardinops_sagax: The Pacific sardine is a small schooling forage fish that can be found in most oceans. It reaches 40cm in length and typically forms massive schools of hundreds of individuals.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.sardinops_melan: The Japanese pilchard is a small schooling forage fish that is found in the Pacific Ocean. It was once considered a synonym of Sardinops sagax but has since been validated as its own species: Sardinops melanosticta.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.sardina_pilchar: The European pilchard is a small schooling forage fish that can be found in the northeast Atlantic, Mediterranean and the Black Sea. They move towards deeper cooler waters during fall and winter, returning to shallower waters when it is warmer.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.congiopodus_tor: The smooth horsefish is a medium sized bottom dwelling fish that has a projected mouth and a tall dorsal fin that extends to its head. They are endemic to temperate waters of southern Africa. Babies have rough skin while adults are smooth, hence the name.
trivia.wildlifeexplorers.tautoga_onitis: The Tautog, also known as the blackfish is a species of wrasse that can be found in shallow waters. They have powerful jaws, allowing them to crush hard shelled prey. Their young take shelter in sea grasses and are green for camouflage.

gui.wildlifeexplorers.holonet.welcome.li: This is a wildlife explorer's catalog of species you discover.
Fish Compendium: True to its name... Fish!
Scan creatures by left or right clicking them.
gui.wildlifeexplorers.holonet.tutorial.s:
Scan living creatures by left or right clicking them. 

Some animals are particularly rare. Good luck trying to find them all!

You do not need to have the Holonet in your hotbar or inventory to scan. You can also open the Holonet with a keybind while it is in your inventory (Default: G)
gui.wildlifeexplorers.holonet.tutorial.g:
A few creatures are able to pass on their traits to their offspring with this system. The Betta fish will be the example here. 

Breeding two different parents will result in children with combined traits. Mutations can also occur at a 10% rate. Some mutatable traits have prerequisite parent traits, while others can appear from any parent trait.
gui.wildlifeexplorers.holonet.tutorial.f:
This device is used to catch small creatures used as breeding items for your other animals. 
All you need to do is place it in water, and insert fish meat or fish food. Then wait as the trap fills up. 

Different critters can be caught in different biomes in this way.
gui.wildlifeexplorers.holonet.tutorial.a:
The Aquarist can setup shop in any village with a Water Trap as their job block! 

They will sell you a multitude of aquaculture-related items including breeding items, raw meats, fish food, and even buckets of fish!
commands.wildlifeexplorers.holonet.inval: %s is not registered in the Holonet.
